resale_co.name: Certificate of Inspection (Property Transfer Application, Division of Housing)
resale_co.issued_by: Township of Lawrence Division of Housing (Housing Bureau)
resale_co.lead_time: Apply as soon as possible after listing; the Township says the current wait for an inspection is about 3-4 weeks (its FAQ says generally within two weeks). No expediting.
resale_co.valid_for: One year from the original inspection date
requirements: Smoke alarms as required for the year the home was built (hard-wired, interconnected alarms for newer homes); battery-only alarms must be 10-year sealed units
Smoke alarms older than 10 years must be replaced
Carbon monoxide alarm within 10 feet of the bedroom doors (or one in each bedroom)
Secondary power source label (generators, solar, batteries) within 18 inches of the main electrical panel and meter, not handwritten
Fire extinguisher is checked during the housing inspection (per the Housing FAQ; the February 2026 checklist no longer lists it)
Dryer vents must be aluminum flex, not plastic
Sump pumps must discharge outdoors, not into the sewer
Private well: well test report under the NJ Private Well Testing Act sent to the Division of Housing
Septic system: NJDEP-protocol septic inspection reviewed and approved by the Health Department before the certificate is issued
A failed septic system or outstanding permits must be addressed by the current owner before closing
Life safety violations must be corrected and reinspected before anyone moves in; a buyer may assume most other violations in writing

fees.label: Certificate of Inspection for a sale (single or two family)
fees.quote: You must complete the application and submit it with the fee of $80.00 to our office.

fees.label: Housing Inspection Fee (Township fee ordinance 2495-25, adopted May 20, 2025)

resale_co.how_to_apply: Fill out the Property Transfer Application and bring or mail it with the $80.00 fee to the Division of Housing, 2207 Lawrence Road (Lawrenceville Road), Lawrence Township, NJ 08648. Faxed or emailed applications are not accepted. Pay by check (payable to Township of Lawrence), exact cash, money order, or Visa/Mastercard credit in the office only. After the application and fee are received, the owner or agent calls the Division of Housing (609-844-7032) to schedule. An adult must be present if occupied; a vacant home with a lockbox can be inspected with the lockbox code. The certificate is typed the next business day and mailed or picked up (not emailed or faxed).
resale_co.contact_title: Fire Prevention Specialist, Division of Housing

evidence.quote: If I am selling my home/condo do I need to get a Certificate of Inspection? Yes, a Certificate of Inspection is required prior to the transfer of ownership.
All single family or two family dwellings being sold are required to file an application of sale with the Housing Bureau, prior to sale.
How long is a Certificate of Inspection for a sale valid for? A Certificate of Inspection expires one year from the original inspection date.
Is there a fee for a re-inspection? No there is no fee for a re-inspection.
Currently the wait time for an inspection is approximately 3-4 weeks.
Can I pay extra to expedite an appointment? No. We do not expedite appointments.
Our office accepts checks, exact cash, money orders or we can accept Visa or Mastercard (credit only, no debit) In the office.
If there is a failed septic system on the property or outstanding permits these must be addressed by the current owner prior to closing.
Applications can be submitted In person or malled to our office. We do not accept faxed or e-mailed applications.
Label must be installed within 18 inches of the main electrical panel and electrical meter warning of dangers associated with secondary power source.
Review and approval by the Health Department is required prior to issuance of a Certificate of Inspection.
Kelly Barkalow , Fire Prevention Specialist Telephone: (609) 844-7032
Email kbarkalow@lawrencetwp.com Phone Numbers 609.844.7032

resale_co.notes: There is no fee for a re-inspection. Lawrence calls the resale certificate a Certificate of Inspection, issued by the Division of Housing (the FAQ explains a Certificate of Occupancy is a construction document). The Property Transfer Application is a December 2020 scan; the Pre-Inspection Checklist is dated February 2026. The seller is normally responsible, but for as-is, bank-owned or foreclosure sales the buyer may be. A separate rental Certificate of Inspection ($75, needed at each tenant change) and a lead-in-rentals program apply to rentals only, not sales. The Housing and Fire Marshal pages both list kbarkalow@lawrencetwp.com as the office email.

requirements: No separate smoke/CO certificate for a sale: smoke alarms, CO alarms and the fire extinguisher are inspected during the Division of Housing inspection and included in the Certificate of Inspection
Battery-only smoke alarms must be 10-year sealed units; alarms over 10 years old must be replaced
Secondary power source warning label within 18 inches of the main panel and meter (homes with generators, solar or batteries)
Low-voltage monitored systems are supplemental; originally required alarms must be put back if removed

fire_cert.notes: Lawrence has one municipal fire code enforcing agency (the LEA registry shows a single 'M Lawrence Township'; no fire districts). The Township fee ordinance (Sec. 156-3(c), Ordinance 2495-25 adopted May 20, 2025) lists state-level smoke/CO certificate fees ($45/$90/$161), but the Housing FAQ says a separate smoke/CO certificate is not needed for a sale because the check is part of the $80.00 Certificate of Inspection. The Fire Marshal page links Edward Tencza to etencza@lawrencetwp.com; the state directory prints ETencza@lawrencetwp.com. The Housing FAQ still says extinguishers are inspected, but the February 2026 Pre-Inspection Checklist (which cites P.L.2025, c.19) does not list an extinguisher.

other_items.label: Open permits
other_items.detail: Outstanding permits must be addressed by the current owner before closing; the application has an Outstanding Permits section. The checklist also tells buyers to verify there are no open permits (records requests go to the Municipal Clerk).

other_items.label: Septic system
other_items.detail: A NJDEP-protocol septic inspection (N.J.A.C. 7:9A-12.6) must be reviewed and approved by the Health Department before the Certificate of Inspection is issued; a failed septic system must be addressed by the current owner before closing.

other_items.label: Private well test
other_items.detail: Homes with a private well must be tested under the NJ Private Well Testing Act; the report should be sent to the Division of Housing.

other_items.label: Buyer assumption of violations
other_items.detail: A buyer may assume most violations with the Assumption of Violations by Buyer letter; life hazard violations must be corrected and reinspected before occupancy.

open_questions: Ordinance 2495-25 prints the lowest smoke/CO tier as '-10 business days'; it likely means 10 or more business days, but the fee does not apply to sales per the Housing FAQ. Confirm with the Fire Marshal's Office when, if ever, the separate smoke/CO fee is charged for 1-2 family homes.
Current inspection wait: the Housing page says about 3-4 weeks while the FAQ says generally within two weeks.
